claims: C1 the example illustrates the no-repetition rule for follow-up code questions
C2 the GOOD response skips preliminaries and explanations covered in the previous message
C3 the BAD response repeats installation instructions
C4 for a follow-up code question, skipping already-covered preliminaries is preferred over repeating them

concepts.name: no_repetition_rule
concepts.gloss: R is subject to the no-repetition rule: the assistant should avoid repeating substantial parts of the user's request or information it has already told the user
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text illustrates the rule without stating it

concepts.name: follow_up_code_question
concepts.gloss: Q is a follow-up question about code, asked after a previous assistant answer on the same topic

concepts.name: previous_message_covered
concepts.gloss: P is a previous assistant message that already covered preliminaries and explanations relevant to the follow-up question

concepts.name: response_skips_preliminaries
concepts.gloss: response R skips the preliminaries and explanations that message P already covered

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.inference: the preference relates a response to the question it answers; the example pairs each assistant response with the user's follow-up question

asserts.read_back: responding with % is preferred: a follow-up code question should be answered by skipping preliminaries and explanations already covered in the previous message
asserts.body: follow_up_code_question(Q), previous_message_covered(P), response_skips_preliminaries(R, P), answers_question(R, Q)

closure.reason: the example states a preference between two permitted responses; it forbids nothing, so silence leaves responses permitted
